newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-KLINSMANN HEADS FOR A YEAR ON THE RIVIERA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN HEADS FOR A YEAR ON THE RIVIERA.

text.p: Juergen Klinsmann signed for Sampdoria on Friday, choosing the Italian Riviera as the backdrop for the sunset of his brilliant career.
The 32-year-old German striker's move from Bayern Munich was announced formally by the north-western serie A club in a short statement that implied a one-year contract.
Klinsmann may not be aware of it, but his signitirely in keeping with the club's history.
In the 1940s and 50s the Genoa side, rarely challengers for the title, were dubbed "Milan's Old Boots".
The tag derived from so many of their players being ex-Milan and Inter stars reaching the twilight of their careers. Sampdoria was where they went to hang up their boots.
Klinsmann was an Inter player in the late 1980s before he travelled further afield to Monaco, Tottenham and Bayern Munich, and Sampdoria should be his European swansong.
But it would be unfair to suggest that the globetrotting German is heading for a gentle last season, a couple of hours' drive south from his lakeside holiday home in Como.
Sampdoria have a young team and while Klinsmann will be the big-name star he will not be held in too much awe.
There have been big names before, including Ruud Gullit who arrived from Milan.
Familiar Italian names include Juventus coach Marcello Lippi, who spent most of his playing career there.
The coach next season looks set to be Argentine Cesar Luis Menotti, a man who has never coached in Italy before but whose achievements have earned him a place in history.
World Cup winning coach in his native Argentina in 1978, Menotti's arrival as replacement for departing Swede Sven-Goran Eriksson will give Sampdoria unique experience.
No other team in Italy can claim to have one World Cup winner on the bench and another on the field.
That should fit in well with Sampdoria's tested strategy of fielding a wise, older player to guide the others.
Veteran Roberto Mancini ably performed the role of team teacher and target-man this season and is now widely expected to confirm his departure with Eriksson to Lazio.
Stepping into Mancini's shoes will not be easy.
The former Italian international, also 32, has been at Sampdoria continuously since 1982 and is the highest scoring Italian player still active in serie A.
This season he has scored 14 times despite injury.
Klinsmann, determined to leave Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich, is just the sort of player that the club need to help get over Mancini's departure, assuming he leaves.
The German, who was a member of the 1990 World Cup winning side, can offer goals and popularity but what he gets in return from Sampdoria is less clear.
The big plus point is sure to be an effective guarantee of first team football alongside young striker Vincenzo Montella, the second highest scorer in serie A this season.
But Klinsmann has probably sacrificed European soccer glory for the chance of a regular spot in the sunshine.
Sampdoria, who looked like title challengers earlier in the year when they beat both Milan and Inter, are seventh.
The UEFA Cup is the most they can hope for and, with three matches left, even that looks uncertain.
